title: The repo-root wrangler manifest is the sole declaration of the Worker's deploy shape
iWant: one file at the repo root that declares the Worker name, entry, compatibility settings, and every binding
soThat: the deploy shape is legible without reading CI scripts or a vendor dashboard

acceptanceCriteria.description: A `wrangler.toml` (or `wrangler.jsonc`) exists at the repo root, parses as valid config, and its top-level object carries `name`, `main`, `compatibility_date`, and every binding block the Worker's runtime code references.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fresh clone of a repo that has applied the blueprint and realised the manifest
acceptanceCriteria.when: a manifest loader parses the file
acceptanceCriteria.then: the loader returns a config object whose `name` is a non-empty string, `main` resolves to an existing entry file, `compatibility_date` matches `\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}`, and every binding name referenced from the Worker's source appears as a declaration key in the config

acceptanceCriteria.description: A CI gate scans the Worker's source tree for references to bindings (env accessors keyed by binding name) and refuses the build when a referenced binding name has no matching declaration in `wrangler.toml`.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a change adds `env.NEW_KV.get(...)` to the Worker source and does not add `NEW_KV` to `wrangler.toml`
acceptanceCriteria.when: the CI gate runs on the change
acceptanceCriteria.then: the run fails with a stable-coded `WRANGLER_BINDING_UNDECLARED` error naming the offending source path and the missing binding name

acceptanceCriteria.description: The manifest never carries a secret VALUE; a source-tree scan across every file that could contribute a bound value at deploy time (the wrangler config, any `.env`-shaped file the deploy step reads, any CI environment block committed to the repo) finds no match for any value the secrets contract resolves.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the secrets contract resolves a set of secret values `V` for the current environment
acceptanceCriteria.when: a redaction-scanner runs against `wrangler.toml`, any committed environment file, and the CI workflows
acceptanceCriteria.then: no file in the scanned set contains any byte sequence in `V`

acceptanceCriteria.description: When the manifest declares an `[assets]` block AND the Worker's fetch handler installs an auth gate on any route whose path could be shadowed by a file under the assets `directory`, the manifest MUST declare `[assets] run_worker_first` naming every gated route (glob-matched); a deployed request to any listed path is answered by the fetch handler before the assets pipeline runs. Without the listing, the assets pipeline serves the shadowing file directly and the auth gate is silently bypassed at the edge.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a Worker whose fetch handler installs an auth middleware on `/notes` and a `./public/notes.html` file present at build time; the deployed Worker is reachable at production URL P
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response is the auth middleware's unauthenticated response (a redirect to sign-in, a 401, or the middleware's declared shape); the response is NOT the byte content of `./public/notes.html`; a manifest that omits `/notes` from `[assets] run_worker_first` fails the deployed observation because the assets pipeline answered before the fetch handler ran
